rows.id: R2-142 / P2: PdfPreview has no watchdog for a pdf.js call that never settles
rows.summary: Every call PdfPreview makes to pdf.js (loading the library, getDocument, getPage, the page render, the page-text read) now has a budget: 20 s, twice that before a document has opened in the session, plus 1 s per page up to 100, on a clock that starts the stage again when it rings 5 s or more late (a page that slept). A stage past it fails the build like any other failure (alert 'Preview failed to render (The preview took too long to draw)', Retry, and the change queued behind it builds at once); its loading task is destroyed, its render tasks cancelled, its canvases shrunk and never given back to the pool (a late paint would draw into them), and what pdf.js settles late is dropped (a document that arrives late is released). A text read that never ends gives those pages empty text and status 'ready', as for a page whose text cannot be read (PERF-5), not a failed render of pages that are painted. Proof, both read to the end: tests run 37419934944 (job 112126810945): 135 tests, 0 fail (the 13 new ones, the existing preview, PDF-worker and keystroke-burst tests, 71-startup-chunks at 0.2 kB to spare, knowledge-docs, dead-code); fail-first run 37420248430 (job 112127795023): '# fail 13' without the fix (all 13 tests of the file), all pass with it.
rows.remaining: The shared pdf.js worker is not replaced after a timeout (the page pictures use it too and destroying it under their documents could leave them waiting), so a Retry after a dead worker waits on the same worker and a reload recovers. Still unbounded inside PdfPreview: render(input) itself (pdfBuild.js's PERF-6 watchdog bounds it on the editor path, but PublicResume.jsx's `import('@/utils/pdfBuild').then(...)` has none for a chunk that never loads) and blob.arrayBuffer() (a local Blob, it settles). A zoom repaint has the budget too; when it runs out the old pages simply stay.

rows.id: R2-142 / P1: the PDF build time of a 200,000-character field (hunt row 142)
rows.summary: The case the hunt row names, one rich-text paragraph of 200,000 characters, was already fixed by typing-freeze 7b (splitHugeBlocks, fa4752b2): on CI it builds in 1.8 s and 49 pages, 1.8-2.0 times as long per doubling of the text (12.7 s in the hunt). The step that still grew faster than its input at the app's level is the PLAIN text field (a company, a skills line, a name, a language, a reference, a letter's recipient): textkit lays one paragraph out in time squared and 7b's cut never saw plain text (25,000 to 100,000 characters took 6.4 to 14 times as long: a name 1.5 to 14.3 s, a company 1.1 to 6.4 s, so 200,000 would pass the worker's 20 s); Text (PdfText.jsx), which every template draws strings with, now cuts a string of more than 12,000 characters into lines of a few thousand, and the running header's render-prop line the same way, while text of 12,000 characters or fewer and children with an element in them reach react-pdf as the very same props. That commit's CI proof was dispatched and NOT read by me (owner's order to wrap up): tests run 37421668759 and fail-first run 37421680884, both on 3773a6d5; see notes for what each should show.
rows.remaining: Thousands of short paragraphs, list items or skills in ONE field still cost pages times nodes, inside react-pdf: resolvePagination -> splitPage lays all the content that follows out again on every page (and once more for the page-number header's render prop, about a third of the time). Measured on CI at 200,000 characters: 2,000 list items of 100 characters 23.4 s (88 pages, over the worker's 20 s budget: Export fails 'took too long' for a document that is only slow), 1,000 items 6.6 s, 1,650 paragraphs of 120 characters 8.8 s; 5,000 paragraphs of 20 characters 33 s at 96,000 characters; no template differs (19 measured). Fixing it means patching @react-pdf/layout: a yarn patch plus a lockfile entry that cannot be made without running yarn, so not at reasonable cost. Recommended product call: cap the blocks (paragraphs plus list items) of one field at about 1,500 with a visible notice like the 200,000-character paste cap, and/or let pdfBuildTimeoutMs count blocks so a slow but sound build is not failed.

Work counts that show the cause (V8 call counts, Classic): Yoga nodes laid out by react-pdf for paragraphs of 20 characters at 12k/24k/48k = 7,836/27,054/101,090 (x3.5 per doubling), isFixed calls 0.69M/4.6M/33.8M; for one 200k paragraph 2,714 nodes. CPU profile of 2,000 bullets: resolvePagination/splitPage 68-71%, of it resolveDynamicPage (the page-number header's render prop forces a second full re-layout per page) 28-36%, relayout of the remaining content 26-34%, splitNodes (a slice and a filter per child) 17% on 1,650 paragraphs. The preview's own part, not measured here: it paints EVERY page at once, so a 49-page document is about 700 MB of canvas at a pixel ratio of 2 (double while the previous pages stay up): a memory risk for very long résumés, not a build time.

NEW BUGS / OBSERVATIONS (not fixed): (1) the PDF worker's budget counts entries, not blocks or pages, so a sound résumé whose layout takes 23 s (2,000 list items in one entry) is failed at 20.25 s and its Export fails too, with no way out; (2) the preview paints all pages at once (see above); (3) tests/pdf/164-huge-paste-linear.test.mjs asserts a wall-clock ratio (flaky by design; the rule is to count work: tests/pdf/175 shows how) and docs/tracking still lists hunt row 142 as open although 7b fixed its case; (4) PublicResume.jsx's render does a bare dynamic import with no bound; (5) PdfPreview exports non-component values (pdfjsTimeoutMs, _setPreviewClockForTest), as it already did with _setPdfjsForTest: Fast Refresh does a full reload on edit in dev; (6) accessibility: none seen, none touched.
